title: Personal Checking: Bank-Error Refunds of Extended Overdraft Fees
content:
## Subject

Personal Checking refunds an extended overdraft fee that was charged in error as a bank-error correction. The obligation is triggered by what the account's records show, not by a customer request, and the question it answers is whether the extended overdraft fee under review is returned in full or not returned at all. A plea for goodwill on an extended overdraft fee that was charged properly is decided by the courtesy refund rules, not by this policy.

## What changes on the account

Once posted, the refund appears in the activity immediately, is labelled a bank-error correction of an extended overdraft fee, and adds its amount to the posted ledger balance straight away.

## Calling the refund tool

Agents reach `refund_extended_overdraft_fee_22b46ecc` by unlocking it from the hidden tool set; it is then called by the agent. A call posts one refund entry dated today that gives back one extended overdraft fee entry in full as a bank-error correction. It books the amount it is handed against the fee it is handed, and it carries out no check of its own on the fee, its date, its amount or previous refunds.

Arguments:

1. `checking_account_id` — which checking account the extended overdraft fee was charged to; use the reference number returned by the checking account lookup.
2. `customer_id` — the owner, identified by the customer reference number returned by the customer profile lookup.
3. `source_item_id` — the extended overdraft fee entry to be refunded, identified by its reference number in the checking activity lookup.
4. `amount` — the U.S. dollar sum to refund; always a positive plain number with two decimal places, rounded half-up, for example 12.34.
5. `statement_cycle` — the statement cycle containing today's posting, written as `YYYY-MM` for the month in which that cycle closes.

What a successful call returns: one sentence confirming the posting. It gives the new refund's reference number and the reference of the extended overdraft fee it answers, then the dollar amount given back and the account's resulting posted ledger balance, both shown with two decimal places. Once it comes back, the refund stands on the account.
